title: The loop can read menus and drive other apps
goal: The loop can now photograph its own copy of the app, but it still cannot read a menu title or send a keystroke to another app, so audits keep leaving those checks for you by hand. This needs one tick in System Settings that only a person can make.
notes: Half of decision the-loop-can-see-the-screen-so-audits-carry-real-may-the-unmanned-loop-take-scree (answered "grant" on 2026-09-02) is still outstanding: Screen Recording for com.dzearing.photonz.probe is granted, Accessibility for Ghoztty is not. Grant path: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility, tick Ghoztty (the app that owns the loop terminal; Scripts/permcheck.swift reports the state, Scripts/probe-app.sh prints it). Apple Events to System Events may need a separate Automation grant, which permcheck reports as unknown while System Events is not running. Blocks audit 2026-09-02-capture-menu-names rough 2.
acceptance: Scripts/probe-app.sh prints Accessibility granted for the terminal that runs the loop.
A runner can read the app menu titles from the running probe and put them in an audit.
The audit that follows this one names a real menu item it read, not one it guessed from the source.
